chunks: And the Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Abi Ja'far, from his father, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad عليه السلام, who said:
Nothing corrupts the water except that which has flowing blood.

key_terms.الْمَاءَ: water used generally, including for taharah
key_terms.سَائِلَةٌ: flowing, meaning blood that gushes or runs
key_terms.نَفْسٌ: a living soul, here meaning an animal life
key_terms.يُفْسِدُ: renders corrupt or impure in legal context

ai.seo_question: What kinds of dead creatures make water impure in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning ritual purity and water. It states that water is not rendered impure except by something from a creature that possesses flowing blood, making it significant in fiqh discussions of najasah and taharah.
